card.title: Tradition Outranks Explanation
card.instruction: Treat inherited customs as meaningful because they have been repeated. Preserve each step and resist every request to explain why it still matters.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Set an empty bowl for Great-Uncle Arthur before we serve dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then he'll finally get to see his bowl.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we put soup in it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not after forty years of keeping it empty for him.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 preserves the inherited empty bowl, A3 treats Arthur's presence as a chance to witness it, and A5 refuses food because the emptiness has lasted forty years.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's Arthur-is-here correction causes A3's see-his-bowl interpretation; B4's soup proposal causes A5's repetition-based refusal.

relationship.evidence: B2 supplies changed circumstances and B4 suggests letting the present person use the bowl normally.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's practical proposal to defend the exact repeated step; escalation remains compact.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a family dinner and a bowl for Great-Uncle Arthur.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's forty-years-of-emptiness answer is earned by B4's soup and makes repetition its own justification.
